newsitem.title: USA: Ohio gov. signs $300 mln school bond authority.
newsitem.headline: Ohio gov. signs $300 mln school bond authority.

text.p: Ohio Gov. George Voinovich announced late Tuesday he approved $300 million of bonds for school building construction assistance to the state's less affluent districts.

The bill signed by the governor Tuesday also creates an Ohio School Facilities Commission and exempts building improvements and construction projects at educational institutions from the state's prevailing wage law.
The schools program became effective with Voinovich's signature and the prevailing wage exemption takes effect 90 days from now.
"This bill is an important step necessary to streamline and expedite the process to fix the schools," Voinovich said in a news release.

The essentially lease-backed bonds will be issued under the housing and state agency authority, as needed, probably over two or three years, said Paolo DeMaria, assistant director of the Ohio Office of Budget Management.
Before Tuesday, $240 million of debt had been authorized for school construction assistance and $140 million to $150 million had been issued, DeMaria said.
The new law permits the state to assist the bottom 5 percent of schools, eliminating old rules that required the state to assist the least able district first, DeMaria said.
There should be no disruption of current projects and after a "lag time" in getting the program operating, needs should be addressed more quickly, DeMaria said.
No new issuance is expected in the short term, DeMaria said.
